entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, offered as a managed cloud platform or Apache-2.0 self-hosted software. It supports semantic, keyword, and entity-based retrieval, with SDKs, a CLI, and a self-hosted server.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight provides long-term agent memory through retain, recall, and reflect operations. It offers Python, Node.js/TypeScript, and Go clients, and supports multiple LLM providers, including local options.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that organizes knowledge, memories, and skills in one filesystem. Directory-scoped retrieval and L0, L1, and L2 context-loading tiers make it a fit for agents that need structured context access.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee builds connected memory from documents, code, and conversations using a self-hosted knowledge graph engine. It supports local text processing without an LLM and includes a CLI for remembering and recalling text.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API, and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, that extracts facts and handles updates, contradictions, and forgetting. Its connectors include Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub, and it offers plugins, an MCP server, and JavaScript and Python API clients.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: Gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent that stores sourced facts and supports corrections and withdrawal. It can share memory across agents, with optional semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents that stores messages and events on sessions and reasons in the background to update peer representations. It can be used through a managed service, local CLI, or self-hosted FastAPI server.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git repo, using Git-like commit, branch, and merge operations to manage a context tree. It offers a React/Ink-powered interactive TUI and REPL, supports 20 LLM providers, and includes 24 built-in agent tools.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes Agents with one pure-Python dependency. It integrates through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK; BEAM results are reported for v3.0.0, while LongMemEval is pending.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto consolidates memories and reconciles conflicting information, then briefs agents with relevant memories before they act. It supports importing and exporting memory through the Open Knowledge Format.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: Memory OS is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that includes vector search and structured facts. It uses local infrastructure with Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, and applies a Ground Truth hierarchy to prioritize injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: AutoContext is a recursive self-improving context harness that runs tasks against evaluation. It keeps useful lessons, discards dead ends, and leaves traces, reports, and playbooks to support agents on complex tasks.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: This Hermes Agent plugin uses a SQLite store and hierarchical DAG to persist messages, with the goal of never losing a message. Its lcm_grep and lcm_recall tools help recover details from past context.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: Deja-vu searches session history already on disk across supported coding agents, helping users find conversations from months ago. It can also resume or continue sessions in another agent and sync between machines without a cloud service.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: This project provides a self-hosted Honcho backend for private, cross-session memory in Hermes Agent. It supports OpenAI-compatible LLM providers and local inference servers, with an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: Signet provides a local-first identity, memory, and secrets layer with portable state across several agent harnesses. It can import files, webpages, and agent conversations, and includes a dashboard for browsing memories and their sources.
entries.plur-ai/plur: Plur stores shared agent memory as plain-text YAML engrams on disk, using an open format for multi-agent systems. It offers local search after a one-time model download, with keyword fallback; its README reports 95.6% R@5 on LongMemEval-S (N=500).
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine that combines BM25 and vector search with rank fusion and cross-encoder reranking. It can generate session handoffs and capture decisions and preferences, with integrations through hooks, MCP, and native agent plugins.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl-Memory keeps long-term agent memory locally in a SQLite file, with FTS5 search and a five-tier schema. Its package family includes an SDK, CLI, Hermes adapter, MCP server, and LangGraph BaseStore.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot optimizes context ordering to support prefix-cache sharing, including for text and multimodal context. Its context index supports reordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling, and it integrates with Hermes Agent, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and OpenClaw.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: This Hermes memory plugin uses an embedded backend by default, with an HTTP backend also available. Its retrieval results include a why_retrieved reason, and it supports contradiction tracking and memory canonicalization.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: This agent-driven CLI maintains a source-grounded Wiki with citations and history, helping agents recall and evolve persistent knowledge across sessions. It does not require embeddings or a vector database.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: AgentCairn stores durable, cross-project memory as inspectable Markdown files with frontmatter metadata, using an Obsidian vault as the source of truth. It uses a local DuckDB cache for hybrid search and retrieval and connects to coding agents through MCP servers and host-specific plugins.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: Flowstate-QMD uses an anticipatory cache that watches agent session logs to prefetch context. It combines local storage with SQLite-vec and GGUF models via node-llama-cpp, and provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack brings Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace together under a single memory owner for Hermes Agent. It uses SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma to manage state and retrieval, then supplies the agent with a purpose-built evidence packet for each query.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep combines BM25 full-text search with ranked graph traversal to retrieve stored information. It can index codebases, URLs, and multimedia with OCR support, while edge tags link notes through navigable, bidirectional relationships.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema token use through local keyword-based ranking and Tool Search support. It integrates as middleware without patching Hermes core on version 0.19 or later, and includes a dashboard for monitoring savings and managing configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS provides a Git-backed context and workflow layer for Claude Code, Codex, and other listed compatible coding agents. Its workflows cover migration, handoffs, and memory proposals, with integrations opt-in rather than enabled automatically.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes memory plugin stores data in a single .lbdb embedded graph database file and supports BM25 keyword search and named graph relationships. Its importance-weighted recall is designed to surface higher-priority memories during context prefetch.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes configured local sources and selected Hermes runtime sources for capability search and routing. It registers five tools for search, retrieval, traversal, feedback, and usage reports, along with pre-LLM-call and session-end hooks.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: Hermes AgentMemory is a pull-model episodic memory plugin that supports immediate event deletion and uses an on-demand summarizer. It also records prefetch operations in a trace.jsonl audit log.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind: Hermes Blind extracts the original goal from the first user turn of a long Claude Code or Codex session, with goals, first-sentence, and full extraction modes. It skips tool output and other non-user-turn records, and does not use a summarizing model or external service.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: The XMemo plugin provides durable cross-session memory for Hermes Agent, using lifecycle hooks for pre-turn recall and session-end snapshots. It also supports continuity across connected agents and uses a local SQLite layer for caching and write-outbox reliability.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: The Exabase plugin integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It offers tools to search and manually store memories, with configurable query expansion and result reranking for retrieval.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: SourceVault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, including semantic search, file reads, and grounded Q&A. Its slash commands cover search, file reads, context, and Q&A, while repo sync and indexed git-history search are also available.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory for Hermes Agent, with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest enabled by default. It offers HNSW approximate-nearest-neighbor, sparse, and FM-index retrieval, and can run through native Rust FFI or an HTTP daemon.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides memory-management and knowledge-graph traversal tools for Hermes Agent, with 17 tools in total. Its hybrid search combines BM25, vector, and graph methods, and it can automatically checkpoint context during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit is a file-based memory-curation loop that works with plain Markdown and produces JSON diffs for review, without a database. Its rot and lint curators flag stale or conflicting facts, while a local Git repository tracks changes and supports reverting them.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers is an agentic skills framework and development methodology built around composable instructions that guide agents through a workflow of specification, design sign-off, planning, and subagent execution. It belongs in this list for its structured software-development process and documentation for installing it across multiple harnesses.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first design and prototyping system that includes skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins. It supports multiple coding agents through skills, CLI, MCP, or runtime adapters, including Hermes Agent.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This project provides structured cybersecurity skills across 34 security domains, with mappings to frameworks including MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3. Its stated compatibility with more than 26 AI platforms makes it a broad security-skills collection for agent use.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: This skill turns natural-language descriptions and real sources into editable draw.io files. Incremental sync preserves manual layout and annotations, and the project also offers a CLI with an optional MCP server.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: Internet Court combines a master router and connector skills with vendored copies of official protocol skills. It also adds verification and dispute resolution, making it a distinct option for agent-to-agent commerce workflows.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: Avoid AI Writing offers separate detect and rewrite modes: detection flags writing patterns without changing the text, while rewriting applies up to two editing passes and verifies when possible. In-place editing is limited to prose files.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw unifies skill libraries across agents, devices, and team members, then uses background evolution to deduplicate skills and improve their quality. It integrates with Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenAI-compatible APIs.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills for Claude Code and agents compatible with agentskills.io. It also maintains session state in the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: This collection provides 822 professional agent skills as plain Markdown files, with listed tasks including writing PRDs and decoding leases. Its installer copies the skill text files, and uninstalling removes them.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: YouTube Skills covers transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction. It is compatible with Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor, and requires a TranscriptAPI key with a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: Hermes Skill Factory watches active workflows to detect and propose reusable skills, then generates both SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds. Slash commands let users manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: Super-Hermes teaches Hermes Agent to generate custom thinking instructions for specific tasks and includes pre-built analytical lenses for various domains. Its reports pair findings with an account of analysis blind spots.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds type-safe agentskills.io support to Pydantic AI, including progressive disclosure and remote skill registries from Git and S3. It also provides tools for bundled resources and scripts, with sandboxed execution to isolate untrusted scripts from the host.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Creates .lit.md documents that weave prose, diagrams, and source code, then extracts runnable files from the documentation with a tangler. Edits to source files can also be synced back into the literate document, keeping code and documentation connected.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design documents and implementation handoffs for Hermes Agent. Lite and Full modes accommodate different project complexity, while a spec review gate evaluates proposals with PASS/FAIL models.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Provides a harness for long-running AI agents, with SQLite storage and event logging through a mechanism kernel. It coordinates agent teams using the SLP cooperative-agent protocol and shares prompt-first working methods as Markdown recipes and skills.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Shares memory across instances through Markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. It also includes a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: Offers Portuguese-language skills for Hermes Agent in SKILL.md format, alongside guides for installation, configuration, and use. The community accepts contributions through forks and pull requests.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Provides prompting guidance for FLUX image and video generation, plus BFL API integration for polling and webhooks. Its FLUX 3 video suite includes eight specialist skills.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Lists nine Chainlink skills that follow the Agent Skills specification, installable with `npx skills add smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills`. The README describes the repository as containing community examples only.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Creates agent instructions from repositories, documentation, and developer discourse, with both automated and step-by-step workflows. It also includes skill testing and export.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Nika describes workflows as intent-as-code in a single file with four verbs, and checks workflows before calling a model. It runs with a model of your choice and verifies each run’s tamper-evident record.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Provides a registry of reusable skills based on the AgentSkills specification, with a Python client and CLI. Skill installation supports recursive dependency resolution, and the project includes commerce features using TON payments.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Supports autonomous execution of long-running, multi-step tasks with real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Built-in checkpoints and rollback procedures help recover safely.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: This Hermes Agent skill manages Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts using WebDAV and CalDAV. It uses HTTPS and Nextcloud App Passwords, and includes a guided script to validate credentials and configure access.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: HermesHub is a community hub for browsing, searching, and installing skills, built around the Agentic Resource Discovery v0.9 specification. Its federated search connects to GitHub and Hugging Face, and it is designed to operate around the clock via Hermes Agent on NVIDIA infrastructure.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Eagle Eye retrieves relevant Hermes Agent skills through five layers, including hard triggers, full-text search, synonyms, and semantic embeddings. By narrowing the skill list before LLM calls, it aims to reduce token use; it can also degrade gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is an ADHD-friendly personal execution system for habits and study blocks, with agent-driven scheduling and system design through an MCP connection. It stores data in a single local SQLite file and includes a React web app and an Expo-based Android app.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard is a read-only code review skill that uses parallel subagents to examine edge cases, adversarial concerns, and integration issues, then consolidates and triages findings. It also runs a deterministic pre-scan with named analysis tools and verifies findings through proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This Hermes Agent skill simplifies code through parallel Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness agents. It supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust, with a tiered application process and an approval gate.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes adapts verified procedures for task decomposition, investigation, and evidence-based checking. It requires evidence gates across multiple stories, provides a protocol for reproduction and causal debugging, and includes a Python goal engine for persistent task state.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: Hermes Cybersec Lab brings cybersecurity skills, tools, and frameworks together for Hermes Agent, including integrations with 28 frameworks and standards. The highlights also list 2,077 skills across multiple repositories and 131+ tools for network work, forensics, and exploitation.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: Skillsdotnet implements agentskills.io in C#/.NET with MCP integration and progressive disclosure through SKILL.md files. It integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading and can automatically register common agent skill directories.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, real-time dashboard for monitoring token costs, session history, and skill analytics. It keeps data access read-only, desensitizes local logs, and offers optional incident alerts through Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: This collection provides plain Markdown agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode, covering workflows such as code review and session management. Skills can be installed by copying a directory or running the bundled installer.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: Creates reproducible demo GIFs for READMEs by generating VHS tape or Playwright recording scripts, then optimizing the GIF to a target size under 8 MB. It supports demos of terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: Searches more than 13,870 MCP servers and 4,384 agent skills, with direct installation commands for discovered tools and plugins. Its CLI and MCP server work with MCP-compatible clients including Hermes, Cursor, and Claude Code.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: Builds Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes. It also monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly to detect field changes.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: Analyzes past agent sessions to identify skill coverage gaps and draft structured improvement proposals. Updates are gated by deterministic, LLM-judge, and regression evaluators, and the tool runs locally using Python’s standard library without daemons or external services.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: Provides Hermes Agent skills for routing file operations with environment-specific path syntax and selecting and verifying existing, project-compatible Python interpreters. It supports native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, and WSL.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Provides agent skills for social data, CRM management, and lead enrichment, with support for Claude Code, Cursor, and other agentskills.io-compliant clients. It also includes an MCP server for browser-based OAuth authentication.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: Offers Hermes skills for transcribing Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, removing common Chinese AI-writing patterns with a rule-based engine, and extracting structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision. The collection also includes an e-commerce materials studio.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: Lets agents list open support bounties, buy ticket context, and submit answers for human review; public wallet earnings records are available. Board creation returns a URL, API key, and USDC deposit addresses.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: Automates USDC payments for HTTP 402 responses and supports Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: Tests agent skills for structure, functionality, and security in isolated Docker containers, then produces cryptographically verifiable certificates using Ed25519 signatures. It also provides a public API for certificate verification and skill submission.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Exposes 191 tools for structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server and includes five ready-to-use workflow skills. It supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands.
entries.parkyucheol-del/alphapipeline: Provides token-risk checks and prediction-market slippage data through an x402 remote MCP, with free MCP discovery and two permanently free onboarding tools. Most tool calls require x402 payment.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: This Hermes Agent skill generates structured Chinese news briefings at multiple geographic scales, from global coverage to street-level updates. It combines core conclusions and action suggestions with user-interest-aware search expansion through semantic memory, making it suited to tailored briefings.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: This project provides an MCP server for Western and Vedic astrology, with deterministic results that can be verified using SHA-256 hashes. Its no-auth endpoint and per-call REST payments via x402 or MPP make it a distinct, verifiable astrology service for AI agents.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: Agentic-MCP-Skill is a progressive MCP client that uses three-layer lazy loading to minimize token usage while incrementally discovering server metadata and tool schemas. Its socket-based daemon keeps connections persistent, making it a distinct fit for Hermes Agent users who want to validate the agentskills.io pattern.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This Nix collection packages AI coding agents and development tools, including Hermes, and is automatically updated daily. Its README provides a `nix run` command for each tool, making it a straightforward option for launching Hermes through Nix.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone collects scripts and notes for running agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, on Android through Termux. It also documents OpenClaw setup and access to Android hardware and UI through Termux:API and Termux:GUI.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This Termux-based installer and guide runs Hermes Agent on Android using a proot-distro Ubuntu environment. It supports interactive model setup, gateway services, shell commands, and external providers or local models via Ollama.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This unofficial community Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with single-writer safeguards for persistent HERMES_HOME storage. It offers direct deployment or operator-ready CRD workflows, plus configurable gateway mode with optional API and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: This one-command installer brings the Hermes AI assistant to Android through Termux or to iOS through iSH. It also integrates Telegram voice and file messaging, and supports scheduled tasks with cron jobs on Termux.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: hermesclaw runs Hermes Agent with hardware-enforced sandboxing through NVIDIA OpenShell. It restricts network and filesystem access at the kernel level and provides configurable security policies for messaging and web search.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying, monitoring, and operating OpenClaw and Hermes agents on Docker or Kubernetes through REST, CLI, and MCP. It includes Helm-based deployment, a credential catalog and LLM provider integrations, and encrypted secrets with AES-256-GCM and mandatory encryption keys.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image that includes mini-swe-agent and the official Hermes installation. It supports persistent state through mounted home directories and building specific Hermes tags with build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This Nix package and NixOS module supports reproducible Hermes deployment with declarative configuration for cli-config.yaml and workspace documents. It combines Nix-managed and CLI-installed skills, and integrates secrets through systemd EnvironmentFiles and sops-nix.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first control plane for operating multiple Hermes Agent instances from one web application, with separate workspaces and identities for each agent. It provides per-agent Telegram and WhatsApp channels and granular policies for tools, paths, and network access.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes OTG is a portable Hermes Agent package that runs from a USB drive or other drive without host installation or registry writes. It includes Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes with isolated data environments, and bundles tools for offline use.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: This project configures Hermes Gateway as a headless, reboot-safe systemd service on Ubuntu and Debian servers. It also supports recurring AI cron jobs and integrates with Nous Portal.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents applies a multi-agent framework to financial trading: fundamental analysts assess company financials and performance metrics, while sentiment analysts aggregate news headlines, StockTwits, and Reddit chatter. Selected analysts work in parallel using their own tools, bringing different kinds of analysis to the trading process.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control provides a self-hosted interface for governing agent registration, task dispatch, memory browsing, and cost tracking. It supports multi-agent workflows through a Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API, with local Node.js installation or Docker deployment.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires is a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent and other named agent tools. It keeps sessions running in the background with tmux and offers sandboxing plus dashboards with diff review.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: This Control Room-first template describes a path from a single Hermes Agent on one VPS to specialist teams and automated workflows. Its level-based architecture uses a task bus for orchestrator-to-specialist delegation and handoffs, and includes skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: SwarmClaw is for building autonomous agent swarms, with support for 23+ LLM providers, durable agent memory, and MCP tool integration. Visual org charts show how agent teams are delegated, setting it apart as a swarm-oriented option.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions offers a single-screen mission control for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work. Its Kanban board tracks task status and review queues, while live streams show agent reasoning and tool execution; proposed task completions require human verification.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized agents across research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. A strict pipeline architecture and Master Orchestrator handle routing and coordination.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local web system for collaboration between Leader and Specialist agents, managing an automated task lifecycle. It uses MCP and ACP for local tool and communication handling, with a real-time web UI for agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: Hermes Agent Metaharness automates outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code. It runs TBLite and TerminalBench-2 evaluations and provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator stages two competing AI companies, orchestrating nine autonomous agents using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning. A real-time dashboard displays agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel implements a local Mixture-of-Agents stack by querying models in parallel and synthesizing their outputs, using Hermes for task routing and tool-calling. It is designed for consumer GPUs, with stated optimization for RTX 4080/5080 hardware and no cloud dependencies.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph builds a full project graph with `codegraph init`, using structural extraction and cross-file resolution across supported languages. Its MCP support makes that pre-indexed code knowledge available to Hermes Agent and other coding agents.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale tracks token usage and costs across Hermes and a range of other coding-agent clients. It offers both a CLI and a visualization dashboard for reviewing that usage.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap records coding-agent API traffic and provides a self-contained HTML viewer for exported trace sessions. It supports clients including Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Cursor CLI, and redacts common authentication headers before recording.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor is a real-time widget for token usage, costs, and rate limits across 46+ AI coding tools, including Hermes Agent. It also shows historical trends and usage breakdowns, with multi-device sync.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design systems and layout guidance through MCP servers to help build UI with AI. It works with Hermes Agent and other listed tools, and is compatible with AI providers that support markdown or general prompting.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes adds an opinionated workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent. Its skills cover product briefs, design handoffs, and implementation, while seven agents span product-lifecycle roles; GitHub integration can enable issue and pull request delivery.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins is a community CLI for customizing the Hermes terminal UI with banner colors, spinners, and ASCII art. YAML-based configuration supports theme creation, with examples including retro DOS and cyberpunk styles.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang is a command-line static linter for AI agent configurations, tool descriptions, and system prompts, using HERM v1.1 scoring. It scans prompts, tool definitions, schemas, and agent files, then reports findings with specific fixes and supported line references.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place describes itself as a social economy for autonomous AI agents. It supports encrypted agent-to-agent messaging via Signal Protocol, identity registration with human-readable @handles, and commerce through Solana-based USDC and SOL payments.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser built for autonomous agent control via MCP. It supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows, and includes a supervisor sidebar for agent approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes-CCC ports the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to Claude Code Channel, where it runs without separate processes or OAuth. It also includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages, organized into permanent knowledge graph and session cache tiers. Its Claude Code plugin can automatically capture and recall context.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: This setup combines RTK and Caveman templating in CLI workflows that it says can save 90–99% of tokens. It also includes 40+ preconfigured skills for finance, DevOps, and research, with automated installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: Ankh.md is a framework for creating scoped Hermes Agents with per-folder configuration and skills. It supports switching between default and scoped agents, with project-local memories, tools, and custom instructions.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: This project automates installation of Hermes Agent and 12+ supporting services, with three deployment tiers ranging from a minimum viable setup to a production stack. It also supports 29 community plugins across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: This migration tool moves OpenClaw data—including SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives—to Hermes. It also maps configurations and credentials to Hermes YAML and JSON formats and sets up systemd gateway services.
entries.observeco/observeco: Observeco monitors multi-agent systems through a native Hermes plugin that exports real-time conversation telemetry. Its two monitoring modes include passive analysis and scheduled active probing, while config-aware baselines help detect performance drift relative to local file changes.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: Hermes Voice adds voice interaction with wake-word support and offline operation without API keys or accounts. It supports 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro, along with adaptive turn-taking and barge-in.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: Hermes Startup provides a local runtime that operates deterministically with zero network access by default. It requires explicit approval for consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer previews, and exact approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: This Hermes memory plugin provides semantic search and multi-dimensional memory storage. It includes tools to search, add, and delete memories, plus a circuit breaker for MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: CC Switch is a cross-platform manager for Hermes Agent and several other agent tools, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, and Gemini CLI. It belongs in this list for its one-click API provider switching and tools to manage MCP, Skills, and Prompts on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: AionUi is a local, open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs, with a built-in agent that offers file access, web search, and MCP tools. Its 21 ready-to-use assistants and support for macOS, Windows, and Linux make it a broad desktop workspace option.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI provides a way to use Hermes Agent from a web browser or phone, with sessions, chat, and workspace files arranged in a three-panel layout. Its file browser includes inline previews, and the project uses Python and vanilla JavaScript with no build step.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: Hermes Desktop is a companion app for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent, using the official Hermes install script. Its GUI covers profiles, sessions, skills, and tools, and it is available from the project website or GitHub Releases.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: Ekko Studio is a Hermes Agent dashboard for chat, session management, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration across Telegram, Discord, Slack, and WhatsApp. It adds shared and group chats, visual workflows, persistent sessions, and tools for files, voice, devices, and agent management; it is available as a desktop app, npm package, or Docker image.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: Hermes Workspace brings chat, a terminal, memory browsing, skills management, and an inspector panel into a web workspace. Its distinguishing features include Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus a file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal.
entries.spacering-net/codeg: Codeg is a collaborative multi-agent coding workspace that aggregates sessions from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other agents as a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can import, search, resume, and hand off sessions, delegate with @, or queue tasks to run in worktrees; the project also includes 15 built-in agents and supports ACP agents.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: This Hermes desktop app is a native Mac workspace that connects directly to Hermes hosts locally or over SSH, using real sessions and a real terminal. It includes views for sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs, along with an embedded terminal for shell access and system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: Hermes-CN-Desktop is a Windows-first desktop app for Hermes Agent, with support for Windows and macOS and native window and process management. Its built-in Hermes-CN-Core kernel includes health checks and updates, while the interface provides chat, memory management, and LaTeX and Markdown rendering.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: This Chromium side-panel extension connects browser context to a local, cloud, or self-hosted remote Hermes gateway. It can attach page context, files, or staged screenshots, and its Chromium-only Hermes Control can operate tabs.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: Hermex is a native SwiftUI iPhone app for driving a self-hosted Hermes agent, pairing with a hermes-webui server. It is a client-only app for iOS 18 and later, so users run the server themselves; the project describes it as free and without analytics or tracking.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: Wesight is a desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, plus custom LLM model routing. Its runtime dashboard tracks token usage and latency, while a live workspace shows code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is an interactive TUI with nine tabs and four selectable color themes. It tracks agent growth, git projects, and cron jobs, and provides a tmux operator view for managing live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: Agent Sessions is a native macOS browser and cockpit for sessions from Hermes and other coding-agent CLIs. It lets you search prompts, responses, tool activity, errors, and supported image references, resume supported sessions in Terminal.app, iTerm2, or Warp, and track Codex and Claude quota usage.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: Hermes Control Interface is a self-hosted web dashboard for the Hermes AI agent stack, bringing together a browser-based terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and agent status. It also offers streaming chat with tool-call visualization, MCP server lifecycle controls, and a ZOO Swarm Monitor for agent health and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: Hermes Desktop OS1 is a native macOS workspace for Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud VMs and SSH hosts. It can automate Hermes Agent installation on fresh cloud computers and includes WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: Hermes Agent Mission Control is a self-hostable dashboard template that connects to a local Hermes agent through a Postgres message bus. Its approval inbox lets users review requests with side effects before they proceed.
entries.liftaris/herm: Herm is an alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard built with OpenTUI for chatting and managing agent sessions. It also includes a kanban board for work and task management, plus controls for profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: Hermes Telegram Mini App is a locally running, mobile-first React SPA dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0. Its terminal chat supports streaming responses and file attachments, while the app also provides Telegram validation and background spawning for up to five agent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: Portable Hermes Agent is a Windows desktop version presented as requiring no installation, Docker, or admin rights. It includes 100 tools across 20+ toolsets, supports cloud AI and LM Studio local models, and has a workflow engine with scheduling, conditions, loops, and parallel execution.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: Hermes UI is a self-hosted assistant interface with a glassmorphic design for chat and real-time log streaming. It also brings together a file browser and task dashboard with management tools for skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI is a process monitoring and configuration dashboard for Hermes. It provides real-time session activity and cost tracking, conversation and skill-source inspection, and read-only views of configuration and environment variables.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: Pan-UI is a self-hosted AI workspace centered on chat, with skills, extensions, memory, profiles, and runtime controls. It includes real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards, a marketplace for skills and MCP servers, and isolated profiles for separate sessions, memory, and API keys.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: Hermes Agent Desktop is a native desktop client for multi-agent work, with collaboration orchestrated across 20 specialized AI agents. It pairs streaming chat and model switching with a visual Skill Store offering 50+ curated one-click installations.
